author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected: its date and description are edited in place under the same validation as booking, updating the existing visit rather than adding a second one, then the owner's record is shown.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a booked visit's correction form shows the form prefilled with that visit's current date and description
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates that same visit in place, adds no additional visit to the pet, and shows the owner's record
A correction with a blank description or a date of today or earlier is refused, the offending field is named, and the form is redisplayed
A successful correction leaves the pet's visit count unchanged
Correcting a visit for a pet that does not belong to the named owner, or a visit that does not belong to the named pet, is refused
non_goals: Cancelling or removing a booked visit stays out of scope (NG-5)

No on-screen entry point to the correction form is added in this scope: the owner detail page gains no edit link; the form is reachable by its address alone. A visible entry point may follow in a later request
notes: Reuse the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template and its visit model attribute, mirroring the booking flow's validation (description required, date later than today). Correction updates in place; the pet must not gain an additional visit record.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Editing a booked visit is a straight application of two patterns this codebase already contains, added to the existing VisitController (system-design Contracts row; Web controller pattern). It needs no new type, module, dependency, or pattern. Every write still flows through the Owner aggregate via OwnerRepository.save — visits are persisted only by cascade from Owner->Pet->Visit (system-design Overview and Persistence sections; confirmed by Read of Owner.java, Pet.java, VisitController.java — IDE oracle not available on this run, so this is the weaker Read/source basis rather than a symbol-resolution citation). The insert-vs-update-in-place branch is exactly PetController.processUpdateForm/updatePetDetails (mutate the existing persisted instance, then save the owner), and Visit already carries an id-based update path via BaseEntity.isNew(), matching the State Machine section's 'branch on isNew() to choose insert vs update'. The one adjustment to the current design: the visit model-attribute loader must become visitId-aware, mirroring PetController.findPet's petId-optional new-vs-existing branch.
integration_points: Add GET and POST @RequestMapping for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit to the existing VisitController; the form already POSTs to its own URL (method=post, no action) and reuses th:object=${visit}, so the template needs no structural change

The @ModelAttribute('visit') loader (currently loadPetWithVisit: always new Visit() + pet.addVisit) must resolve the EXISTING visit when a visitId path variable is present and return it WITHOUT calling addVisit; when visitId is absent (the /new routes) it keeps today's create-and-add behavior. This mirrors PetController.findPet handling petId==null vs present

Owner->Pet scoping already exists via owner.getPet(petId) (throws IllegalArgumentException when the pet is not the owner's); visit->pet scoping needs a lookup of the visit within pet.getVisits() by id, throwing the same IllegalArgumentException when absent. Cleanest is a Pet.getVisit(Integer) accessor mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) — a navigation query, not a business rule

On successful edit, mutate the resolved existing Visit's date/description (form binding does this once the loader returns the persisted instance) and call owners.save(owner); redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. Do not call pet.addVisit on the edit path

patterns.description: insert-vs-update-in-place: GET initUpdateForm + POST processUpdateForm/updatePetDetails mutate the existing persisted child and saveAndFlush the owner aggregate. The visit edit is the structural twin of this
findPet: petId required=false -> new Pet() when absent, load existing when present. The visitId-aware loader follows this exactly
getPet(Integer): aggregate-navigation lookup by id; Pet.getVisit(Integer) should mirror it

risks.risk: THE load-bearing trap: if the shared @ModelAttribute('visit') loader is left unchanged (always new Visit() + pet.addVisit), the edit routes both attach a spurious transient visit to the pet AND bind form values onto the wrong (new) instance — failing both 'no additional visit' and 'update in place' acceptance criteria at once
risks.mitigation: Make the loader visitId-aware and, on the edit path, return the existing visit resolved from pet.getVisits() without adding a new one; bind and save mutate that persisted instance so JPA issues an UPDATE (Visit.isNew()==false), adding no row

risks.risk: Attempting to carry visitId through the form/body would collide with the mass-assignment guard: the InitBinder disallows 'id' and '*.id'
risks.mitigation: Resolve the existing visit from the trusted @PathVariable visitId only, never from a bound field — this is the intended use of the existing disallowed-fields guard and keeps identifier handling trusted

risks.risk: Validation must reuse the existing rules only; adding a fresh business rule to the controller would be a new violation of the Web controller pattern (architecture-principles catalog), not covered by the recorded deviation
risks.mitigation: Reuse @Valid Visit (@NotBlank description) plus the identical non-future-date check already in processNewVisitForm; add no new rule

notes: Verdict minor, not covered: one adjustment to the current design (visitId-aware visit loader) plus a small doc edit. Updated docs/system-design.md Contracts row for VisitController to add REQ-VIS-003 and note in-place correction. No ADR warranted — no hard-to-reverse or novel decision; every choice reuses an in-force pattern. No design-doc-autofix records present, so the autofix audit was a silent skip.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Pet.getVisit(Integer) throws IllegalArgumentException when the visit is not found, but the twin method it mirrors — Owner.getPet(Integer id) — returns null and documents 'or null if none found'. The call site in loadPetWithVisit relies on the thrown exception rather than a null check, which produces the correct runtime behaviour, but the divergence from the established convention in the same aggregate is an undocumented style inconsistency that a future reader comparing the two will need to reason through. Fix: either (a) have getVisit return null and add an explicit null check and IAE throw in loadPetWithVisit — matching the Owner.getPet caller pattern — or (b) update the Javadoc to say 'throws IllegalArgumentException' and note the deliberate deviation from Owner.getPet.
findings.fix: Preferred: update the Javadoc on Pet.getVisit to document that this method throws rather than returns null, and add a sentence explaining it is deliberately stricter than Owner.getPet because the controller has no separate null-check guard at this call site. Alternatively, change the method to return null and add the null-check block in loadPetWithVisit mirroring lines 71-74.

findings.description: The Javadoc on loadPetWithVisit is stale after the visitId-aware extension. '@return Pet' is wrong — the method returns a Visit. '@param petId' is the only parameter documented but visitId was added. The inline comment block at lines 78-83 captures the new logic correctly, but the method-level Javadoc now contradicts the signature and understates the contract.
findings.fix: Update the Javadoc: correct '@return Pet' to '@return Visit', add '@param visitId the id of an existing visit to resolve on edit routes, or null for new-visit routes', and extend the goals list with a third goal describing the visitId-aware branch.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The init() fixture was modified in this slice to seed a visit with an id, date, and description, but production types are still constructed with bare new Owner(), new Pet(), and new Visit() calls. The brief (§ Test Data Construction) states: 'A slice touching a test moves that test's construction behind a factory.' All three constructions in the modified init() must be extracted to factory methods (e.g. createOwnerWithPet(), createExistingVisit()) so that a future constructor-signature change requires updating one factory instead of every fixture.
findings.fix: Extract createOwnerWithPet() returning an Owner with one Pet whose id is set, and createExistingVisit(int id, LocalDate date, String description) returning a fully-set Visit. Replace the init() body with calls to these helpers.

findings.description: TEST_VISIT_ID is a constant introduced in this slice. Per the three-tier data naming convention (§ Three-Tier Data Naming Convention), a scaffolding ID that has no bearing on the test outcome is a Tier 2 value and must carry an SOME_ or ANY_ prefix. The pre-existing TEST_OWNER_ID and TEST_PET_ID are prior debt excluded from this finding; TEST_VISIT_ID is new and must comply from the start.
findings.fix: Rename TEST_VISIT_ID to SOME_VISIT_ID everywhere it appears in the file.

findings.description: theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheExistingVisitInPlace issues two separate assertThat(savedVisit.getX()) calls on the same object. The checklist (§ Assertions) prefers chained assertions on the same subject. Use assertThat(savedVisit).extracting(Visit::getDate, Visit::getDescription).containsExactly(correctedDate, "Corrected description") or a satisfies block to keep both assertions anchored to one assertThat call.
findings.fix: Replace the two assertThat calls with a single chained assertion on savedVisit using extracting or satisfies.
